runs.text: The document reports no dissolution of PVDF by ethylene glycol. It states that the PVDF binder was
not removed or dissolved during the EG-based separation process

support.quote: not removed or dissolved during the EG-based separation

runs.text: . The FTIR and EDX results are cited as confirmation that PVDF remained on the cathode. The authors explain this with Hansen solubility parameters: EG has a high HSP distance (Ra) from PVDF, which indicates a lower ability to dissolve PVDF.

The document therefore gives no percentage or amount of PVDF dissolved by EG; the answer is effectively none. Delamination was instead attributed to competitive inhibition of PVDF binding through hydrogen bonding.

rendered: The document reports no dissolution of PVDF by ethylene glycol. It states that the PVDF binder was not removed or dissolved during the EG-based separation process[1]. The FTIR and EDX results are cited as confirmation that PVDF remained on the cathode. The authors explain this with Hansen solubility parameters: EG has a high HSP distance (Ra) from PVDF, which indicates a lower ability to dissolve PVDF. The document therefore gives no percentage or amount of PVDF dissolved by EG; the answer is effectively none. Delamination was instead attributed to competitive inhibition of PVDF binding through hydrogen bonding.[2]
